carbon_policy_signal.item: EU extends free pollution allowances for industry to 2040s amid electrification push; ETS scarcity relief.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Extended free allocation reduces carbon cost embedded in power generators' merit-order calculation; dampens fuel-switch incentive and compresses Cal+1 power spreads 2–4% over months.

freshness_caveat: Coal data stale (206 days, as of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark stale (201 days, as of 2025-12-31) — thermal merit-order moves post-year-end unmeasured; impact immaterial to intraday but limits seasonal fuel-switch granularity.
risk_flags: Coal data stale (206 days old, 2025-12-26); Clean Dark stale (201 days, 2025-12-31) — thermal merit-order moves unmeasured post-year-end.
Storage 15.5 pp below seasonal norm at 53.67% — refill pace this summer will set H2 gas risk and power/coal switching regime.
Strait of Hormuz two-thirds capacity; Brent elevation supports OCGT call and TTF arb, but EU oil-cap sanctions unresolved (next week negotiation) — binary Brent move risk ±5–8%.
ETS rule-loosening extends industry free allowances to 2040s — embedded carbon cost falls, dampening fuel-switch urgency and pressuring Cal+1 power 2–3% lower over weeks.

base.summary: GB power remains elevated on Hormuz risk and renewables dip; ETS loosening gradual bearish drift.

downside.summary: Hormuz traffic normalizes; ETS loosening accelerates; record LNG supply arbs to TTF; demand softens.

upside.summary: Hormuz escalation forces OCGT dispatch surge; EU oil price-cap talks collapse, Brent +7–10%.

themes: Geopolitical oil premium lifts power fuel costs
ETS loosening weakens carbon scarcity; bearish curve
Renewables at 92nd-percentile compress DA; storage 15.5 pp below seasonal
GB-DE spread sustained on island isolation and demand
top_drivers: Hormuz supply curtailment (two-thirds capacity) keeps Brent elevated and OCGT profitable; TTF arb margin sustained.
Renewables at 92nd-percentile (68.66% of load) compress DA power; GB isolation (98th-percentile) reflects island wind outages and demand inelasticity.
ETS loosening (extended free allowances to 2040s) removes carbon scarcity signal; Cal+1 power spreads under structural downward pressure despite thermal strength.
Storage 15.5 pp below seasonal (53.67% full) will constrain summer refill; H2 gas risk front-loaded if no Hormuz de-escalation or demand softening.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 98th-percentile on Hormuz supply risk and renewables pullback; Clean Spark at 93rd-percentile signals sustained thermal tension despite loose ETS policy.

watchlist.why: Two-thirds flow rate; any escalation reopens 5–10% Brent upside; OCGT and TTF arb transmission direct.

watchlist.metric: EU Russia oil price-cap negotiation (next week)
watchlist.why: If cap rises, Brent +5–8%; power-plant fuel cost spikes. If stalls, volatility persists and TTF upside risk stretches.
Free allocation extension to 2040s reduces carbon cost embedded in power merit order; Cal+1 spreads compress 2–4% on lower fossil dispatch incentive.
At 53.67% and 15.5 pp below seasonal; slow refill = tight H2 gas regime, reversing LNG dampening and supporting TTF upside Oct-onwards.
US capacity expansion + arbitrage relief dampen TTF; bearish power curve unless Hormuz escalates or European demand surges on electrification.

watchlist_dated.name: EU Russia oil price-cap ratchet decision
watchlist_dated.why: Outcome determines Brent floor and OCGT call magnitude; 5–8% upside or +risk asymmetry.
